mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of YoY GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals a deepening labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary environment, where monetary tightening fails to curb inflation and growth slows, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average, combined with a concurrent rise in personal savings (RSAFS), signals a housing demand recovery, which boosts construction and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month MA and RSAFS > 6-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 6-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its trend for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > trend for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-trend PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals reduced household buffer and higher borrowing, which increases vulnerability to shocks and reduces consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent below-trend RSAFS.
